competitive_position.claim: Okeanis operates a modern, fuel-efficient Eco fleet of 16 tanker vessels (eight Suezmax, eight VLCC) with an average age of 6.4 years and carrying capacity of approximately 3.5 million deadweight tons, giving it a cost and regulatory-compliance edge over older-fleet competitors.
quotes: We are an international owner and operator of a modern, fuel-efficient Eco fleet of 16 tanker vessels, comprising eight modern Suezmax tankers and eight modern VLCC tankers, focusing on the transportation of crude oil.
Our fleet has a carrying capacity of approximately 3.5 million deadweight tons and an average age of 6.4 years as of December 31, 2025

competitive_position.claim: The company's vessels are built to Eco standards with exhaust gas cleaning systems and ballast-water treatment compliance, differentiating them from conventional tankers in a tightening regulatory environment.
quotes: Our vessels are built in line with Eco standards that consume less bunker fuel than conventional tanker vessels, are equipped with exhaust gas cleaning systems ("scrubbers") and are built to comply with regulations for ballast water treatment.

competitive_position.claim: Okeanis competes for charters on price, vessel location, size, age, condition, and operator reputation in a highly fragmented ownership market.
quotes: We will compete for charters on the basis of price, vessel location, size, age, and condition of the vessel, as well as on our reputation as an operator.
Ownership of tankers is highly fragmented and is divided among major oil companies and independent vessel owners.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $391,548,819, a slight decline from $393,229,831 in 2024, while profit for the year rose to $122,951,543 from $108,863,270.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5.A Results of Operations)
competitive_position.claim: Daily Time Charter Equivalent Rates were $52,823 in 2025, marginally below $52,898 in 2024, reflecting spot-market employment of the fleet.
quotes: Daily Time Charter Equivalent Rates decreased to $52,823 for the year ended December 31, 2025, from $52,898 for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to the spot employment of the fleet.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 (Item 4.A History and Recent Developments)
competitive_position.claim: The company is actively expanding its fleet: two newbuilding Suezmax vessels (Nissos Piperi and Nissos Serifopoula, $97.0 million each) were delivered in January 2026, two VLCCs (Nissos Rhenia and Nissos Despotiko, $94.2 million aggregate) are expected in Q2 2026, and two additional newbuilding Suezmaxes ($99.3 million each) are under construction for Q2 2026 delivery.
quotes: In January 2026, we received delivery of our newly acquired vessels, the Nissos Piperi and the Nissos Serifopoula.

In October and November 2025, we exercised our purchase options for two VLCC tankers, the Nissos Rhenia and Nissos Despotiko (both built in 2019), respectively, currently on lease from OCY Knight 1 Limited and OCY Knight 2 Limited. The two ships are expected to be delivered to us during the second quarter of 2026, for an aggregate consideration of $94.2 million.

In January 2026, we entered into two memoranda of agreement, whereby pursuant to each individual memorandum of agreement, we agreed to purchase one newbuilding Suezmax vessel (with an estimated approximate deadweight tonnage of 157,000) (the "Additional Vessel Acquisitions"), currently under construction at Daehan, from an unrelated third-party seller for an acquisition price of $99.3 million each.

competitive_position.claim: The Baltic Dirty Tanker Index was highly volatile in 2025 (high 1,468, low 799) and stood at 2,850 as of March 17, 2026, meaning charter revenue is exposed to sharp swings in both directions.
quotes: in 2025, the BDTI reached a high of 1,468 and a low of 799. Although the BDTI was 2,850 as of March 17, 2026, there can be no assurance that the crude oil charter market will continue to increase, and the market could again decline.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (Item 3.D Risk Factors), citing BIMCO
competitive_position.claim: The crude tanker newbuilding orderbook hit a nine-year high of 14.1% according to BIMCO in November 2025, signalling future capacity growth that could compress charter rates.
quotes: according to BIMCO in November 2025, the crude tanker newbuilding orderbook hit a nine-year high of 14.1%. If the capacity of new vessels delivered exceeds the capacity of tankers being scrapped and converted to non-trading tankers, tanker capacity will increase.

competitive_position.claim: Geopolitical conflicts—Ukraine-Russia war, the February 28, 2026 US/Israel strikes on Iran killing Ayatollah Khamenei, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, and instability in Venezuela—create both rate volatility and physical risk to tanker operations, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz.
quotes: on February 28, 2026, the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran, killing Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei.

shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway essential to the shipment of crude oil and refined petroleum, may experience prolonged disruption. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has warned vessels to avoid the passage.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (Item 3.D Risk Factors), citing IEA Global EV Outlook 2025
competitive_position.claim: The IEA projects global oil demand will peak around 2030 before gradually declining, and 25% of all new cars sold in 2025 are expected to be electric, posing a long-term structural threat to tanker demand.

a total of 25% of all new cars sold are expected to be electric in 2025, up from 18% in 2024
